data.title: Guru's daily horoscope for Oct 4
data.description: The day of the week you were born on can reveal a lot... Read on.

data.title: Wake-up call! Forward Kristensen's double rocks rotated Thailand
data.description: Thailand's preparations for the Fifa Asean Cup final suffered a jolt on Friday night, when a heavily rotated side lost 2-1 to the Philippines in their final Group B fixture at Si Jalak Harupat Stadium in Bandung.

data.title: Phuket festival to draw 140k locals
data.description: PHUKET: The annual nine-day Vegetarian Festival is expected to attract about 140,000 local tourists and generate more than 1.3 billion baht in local spending, the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) says.

data.title: Rider accused of B3.7m theft
data.description: PHUKET: Police have arrested a food delivery rider accused of stealing cash and camera equipment worth more than 3.69 million baht from two foreign residents' homes in Muang district.

data.title: Another slice of history for teen Thai skater Hiro
data.description: Hiro Kaewtathip made history again by winning Thailand's first-ever gold medal at the ISU Figure Skating Junior Grand Prix.

data.title: Star Puripol crowned the Asiad MVP
data.description: Star sprinter Puripol Boonson has been selected by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) as the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the 20th Asian Games after delivering a spectacular performance on the track in Japan.

data.title: Floods won't disrupt IMF meetings, ministry says
data.description: Flooding will not disrupt the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group in Bangkok on Oct 12-18, and evacuation plans are ready if water levels rise, the Finance Ministry says.

data.title: BMA dropped ball on floods: Uni
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) failed to respond to advance warnings of a potential flood crisis, climate expert Assoc Prof Seree Supratid said.

data.title: Media urges safeguards for Thai PBS
data.description: Six media organisations have called for legal and financial safeguards to protect Thai Public Broadcasting Service (Thai PBS) independence after a Bhumjaithai Party bill proposed changing its funding to annual state budget allocations.

data.title: Suphajee keeps eye on traders
data.description: Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun has ordered strict price checks and stock monitoring to prevent traders from exploiting consumers affected by flooding.

data.title: Call for better teen parent support
data.description: The government must redesign support systems for teenage parents, addressing gaps in welfare, healthcare and laws to tackle complex problems they may face, the Sexualities Studies Association says.

data.title: Currency shifts boost tourism in the South
data.description: A stronger Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar are boosting tourism in Hat Yai and Dan Nok in Songkhla province, with Chinese tourists based in Malaysia among high-spending visitors.

data.title: Govt, BMA under fire for response
data.description: The Bangkok floods have exposed failures in preparedness, warning systems and coordination, with analysts pointing to deeper structural weaknesses in crisis management.

data.title: Govt urges 60/40 co-payment sign-ups before deadline
data.description: More than 22.3 million beneficiaries have confirmed their eligibility for the government's expanded Thais Help Thais Plus (60/40) co-payment scheme, and the government is urging those who have yet to register to do so before the Oct 15 deadline.

data.title: Flood, disaster response 'weak'
data.description: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has proposed structural reforms to the water management system, including unified flood command and proactive disaster funding.

data.title: Govt plays down cost of floods
data.description: The Finance Ministry estimates the floods will have an impact of less than 0.1% on the overall economy, maintaining its forecast of 2-2.5% GDP growth for 2026.

data.title: Israel targets top Hamas leader in deadly Gaza strike on anniversary
data.description: GAZA CITY (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Israel said on Saturday that it attempted to kill Hamas's top leader in the Gaza Strip in an airstrike on an apartment that local officials said killed five people, four of them women.

data.title: Houthis say Saudi Arabia launches dozens of strikes on Yemen capital
data.description: SANAA - Yemen's Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of launching dozens of strikes on Sanaa on Saturday, while an AFP journalist in Riyadh reported seeing flames and smoke coming from an oil facility on the outskirts of the Saudi capital.

data.title: UAE: flydubai co-pilot was planning ‘terrorist act’
data.description: DUBAI - Investigators in the United Arab Emirates have said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel this week was planning a “terrorist act” and used the cockpit’s emergency axe to attack the captain, but they did not reveal his motive.

data.title: Russia warns diplomats to leave Kyiv before ‘massive’ strikes
data.description: KYIV - Russia on Saturday issued a new call for diplomats and foreigners to leave Kyiv, warning the Ukrainian capital of new “massive” air attacks hours after striking another major bridge in the city.
